text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- An administrative court system set up six months ago to deal with citizen's complaints against government bodies is failing to work.
-- Vietnam's population will swell to 135-140 million by the middle of next century even if the policy of two children per family is maintained.
-- Argentina's President Carlos Menem will arrive in Hanoi on Sunday for a three-day official visit at the invitation of Prime Minister Vo Van kiet.
-- 82 people were killed and 240 injured in traffic accidents over a five-day period during the Tet lunar new year festival.
-- Eleven people including two 14-year-old children were killed when a boat sank in the central coastal province of Ha Tinh last week.
-- The government is encouraging private traders to buy paddy and sell it on to exporters in order to help the country's rice farmers and increase export potential.
-- 34 foreign investment projects with total capital of more than $596.5 million were licensed in January.
